question: A
title: Affordable Housing
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $22 million for affordable housing and related property acquisition, rehabilitation, construction, assistance, and improvements.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for the specified purposes. Authorization alone does not establish which projects receive funding or when money is spent.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: B
title: School Facilities
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $60 million for school buildings, equipment, athletic facilities, and related community health and recreation facilities.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for the specified facilities and related costs.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: C
title: Community And Economic Development
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $50 million for its economic development program, including neighborhood improvements, blight reduction, housing assistance, business support, and other eligible projects.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount and use it for the purposes described in the question, including eligible loans and grants.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: D
title: Public Infrastructure
explanation: Authorizes Baltimore City to borrow up to $148 million for public infrastructure, including city buildings, libraries, parks, streets, utilities, technology, and related improvements.
if_for: The city may borrow the authorized amount for eligible infrastructure and related costs.
if_against: This question would not authorize the proposed borrowing.

question: E
title: Contract Bidding And Awards
explanation: Removes charter provisions requiring lowest-bid awards, governing tied bids, and specifying certain bid and performance bonds. Those subjects could instead be governed through ordinances or regulations.
if_for: The charter provisions would be removed on November 7, 2028, unless a relevant ordinance or regulation takes effect sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions on contract bidding and awards remain.

question: F
title: Budget Process And Board Of Estimates
explanation: Changes legislative deadlines and the budget process, transfers financial responsibilities from the Board of Estimates to other city officials or bodies, removes the preliminary budget hearing process, and removes the charter’s $1 million emergency contingency-fund cap.
if_for: The changes take effect on different dates: December 3, 2026 for most changes, December 5, 2028 for legislative approval and veto changes, and November 7, 2028 for removed sections unless replaced sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions governing legislation, the budget, and the Board of Estimates remain.

question: G
title: Franchises And Minor Privileges
explanation: Protects the city’s stormwater system from sale or franchise rental, clarifies that conduit space may be rented while the conduit system cannot be sold, and revises permissions for certain uses of city property.
if_for: An executive agency could grant minor privileges under a process established by ordinance. Most changes take effect December 3, 2026; removed sections take effect November 7, 2028 unless replaced sooner.
if_against: The existing charter provisions on franchises and minor privileges remain.

question: H
title: Department Of Water And Wastewater
explanation: Creates a separate Department of Water and Wastewater, transferring water and wastewater responsibilities from Public Works. It also removes the charter requirement that Public Works bureaus be established or abolished by ordinance.
if_for: The charter changes take effect January 1, 2029.
if_against: The existing charter provisions governing water and wastewater systems remain.

question: I
title: Baltimore Baby Fund
explanation: Creates a separate fund to support the economic stability of Baltimore families with newborns. It requires an annual city contribution tied to taxable property value and allows grants and donations.
if_for: The city must contribute an amount equivalent to $0.03 per $100 of taxable property value annually. Fund money cannot replace existing newborn funding or be transferred to unrelated purposes.
if_against: The proposed fund would not be established by this amendment.
